profile.name: Bruckins
profile.tagline: A stately, dipping-gliding Jamaican Emancipation pageant in royal costume.
profile.insight: Performed to celebrate Emancipation, dancers dress as European royalty in an elaborate pageant blending European and African musical elements.
profile.profile: Bruckins, also spelled brukins, is a Jamaican dance performed primarily to celebrate Emancipation Day. The dance is described as a "stately, dipping-gliding" form that may be derived from the Pavane. Its music incorporates both European and African elements. Participants accompany the dance with an elaborate pageant, dressing as European royalty, courtiers, pages, and soldiers.
profile.profile_long:
Bruckins, also spelled brukins, is a Jamaican dance performed primarily to celebrate Emancipation Day. Historical accounts of its origin vary; Sabine Sörgel states that the first Bruckins was celebrated in 1834 after the formal abolition of slavery, whereas Olive Lewin states that it was first celebrated in 1839 following the elimination of the apprenticeship system. The dance is characterized as a "stately, dipping-gliding" movement and may be derived from the Pavane.

The performance is accompanied by an elaborate pageant where participants dress as European royalty and members of the royal court, including courtiers, pages, and soldiers. Musically, the dance incorporates both European and African elements. Because the available sources are extremely thin, detailed documentation regarding footwork, instrumentation, and regional variants remains limited.
